extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funding (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, compliance officers, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards governing when and how an education recipient may offer and conduct informal resolution of complaints alleging sex discrimination under Title IX, including required safeguards, notice, consent, and limits (particularly for minors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to offer informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may offer an informal resolution process to a complainant and respondent, subject to the limitations in §106.44(k)(1). The recipient has discretion to determine whether informal resolution is appropriate when it receives information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretion must be exercised in a manner that treats the parties equitably (consistent with §106.44(f)(1)(i)). The recipient's discretion is not unfettered — it is subject to guardrails in §106.44(k) (e.g., voluntariness, notice, prohibition for certain employee-to-minor allegations). The recipient may decline informal resolution based on fact-specific considerations (nature of allegations, identity of parties, risk of future harm, repeated allegations, ability to exert control). A recipient is not required to provide written reasons for declining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition for employee sex-based harassment of elementary/secondary students
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal resolution is prohibited if the complaint includes an allegation that an employee engaged in sex-based harassment of an elementary school or secondary school student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule limits the prohibition to sex-based harassment of minors given heightened risk of physical harm and severe emotional trauma, and retains informal resolution availability for most postsecondary student complaints (including student-employees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary consent; no requirement or pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal resolution cannot be pursued unless both parties voluntarily consent; a recipient must not require or pressure a party to participate in informal resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure voluntariness and guard against coercion or pressure (positive or negative). The Department declined to require a specific form (e.g., written consent) but trustees the recipient to obtain voluntary consent and document as appropriate. For minors, special protections apply (parents/guardians rights, obligations under laws on sexual abuse of minors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitators free from conflict of interest or bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators and informal resolution facilitators must be free from conflict of interest or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement prevents a recipient from using informal resolution to protect a particular party or the recipient's own interests (financial, reputational, or other). Recipients must ensure facilitators do not have conflicts or prejudicial biases; facilitators should be trained (see related criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirement for informal resolution facilitators
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal resolution facilitators must be properly trained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble cites consistency with research on best practices and restorative justice; commenters urged formal training requirements. Recipients are expected to ensure facilitators receive appropriate training and to structure processes consistent with best practices (e.g., skilled facilitation, shuttle negotiation, restorative practices as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements prior to initiating informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Before parties agree to informal resolution, the recipient must provide notice describing the allegations, the requirements of the informal resolution process, the right to withdraw and resume grievance procedures prior to an agreed resolution, the effect of entering into a resolution agreement, potential terms of an agreement, and what information will be maintained and could be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice should explain differences between informal resolution and grievance procedures, timeframes, that informal resolution is optional, and that any agreement is binding only on the parties. The recipient must avoid disclosing personally identifiable information except as permitted by §106.44(j). The Department modified §106.44(k)(3)(v) and (vi) to clarify these points and deleted more prescriptive proposed paragraphs that raised implementation concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information maintenance and disclosure transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must explain to the parties what information related to informal resolution it may maintain and whether and how it could disclose such information if grievance procedures are initiated or resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This balances parties' need to understand consequences of informal resolution with recipient flexibility. The Department struck provisions that would have overly restricted or promised absolute confidentiality; instead recipients must notify parties about recordkeeping and circumstances under which information may be used in later grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to withdraw and resume grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party has the right to withdraw from the informal resolution process and to initiate or resume the recipient's grievance procedures prior to agreeing to a resolution at the conclusion of the informal resolution process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This right must be clearly communicated in the notice and is intended to protect parties' autonomy. An agreed informal resolution at conclusion precludes initiating or resuming grievance procedures for the same allegations, but future discriminatory conduct would not be covered by a past informal resolution agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution agreements binding only on the parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must be advised that an informal resolution agreement is binding only on the parties to that agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must prevent facilitators or parties from offering or agreeing to terms that depend on non-parties' actions (e.g., requiring training of persons who are not parties). Notice should clarify the general framework and parameters rather than list every possible measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and recordkeeping of informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must document and retain records of the informal resolution process under §106.44(k) and include those records among documents retained under §106.8(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents recipients from avoiding a formal record of sex discrimination by steering parties to informal resolution. Recipients cannot use informal resolution to evade recordkeeping obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No waiver of right to investigation/determination as condition of enrollment or employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not require waiver of the right to an investigation and determination of a complaint as a condition of enrollment, continued enrollment, employment, or continued employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation must be voluntary and not a prerequisite for access to education or employment. The recipient may structure the order of offers but cannot condition fundamental rights on acceptance of informal resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for declining informal resolution (illustrative, non-exhaustive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may decline to offer informal resolution in circumstances such as evidence of actual or potential coercion, an ongoing threat of danger to others, a respondent posing an immediate risk of harm to others, a history of violent conduct, credible threats of self-harm or harm to others, repeated allegations against the same respondent, or other fact-specific considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(k)(1)(ii) is illustrative (language: 'include but are not limited to'), not exhaustive. Recipients have flexibility to structure their own assessments and processes to determine future risk; the Department expects fact-specific inquiries tailored to allegations and parties' identities and the recipient's ability to exert control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special protections for minors and parental/guardian rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Elementary and secondary school students (minors) are in a special position and may be especially vulnerable to pressure; nothing in Title IX or regulations derogates parents'/guardians' legal rights to act on behalf of a student in matters including participation in informal resolution (subject to §106.6(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of minors' vulnerability and mandatory reporting/legal obligations regarding sexual abuse of minors, the rule prohibits informal resolution where an employee is alleged to have engaged in sex-based harassment of a minor and ensures additional safeguards to protect minors from coercion.
